thread:
Sam Support: FYI FinEdge is seeing 429s at each minute boundary since ~09:12 UTC. They enabled a per-minute heartbeat on ingestion clients.
Sam Support: Paste of their log:
Sam Support: ```
[2026-03-17T09:12:00Z] upstream POST /v1/generate 200ms 429 rate_limited tenant=finedge rpm=642 tpm=12054 window=60
[2026-03-17T09:13:00Z] upstream POST /v1/generate 190ms 429 rate_limited tenant=finedge rpm=615 tpm=12400 window=60
[2026-03-17T09:14:00Z] upstream POST /v1/generate 220ms 429 rate_limited tenant=finedge rpm=630 tpm=12530 window=60
```
Priya Eng: thx. can you confirm current quota for that tenant and whether any recent quota updates happened?
Sam Support: ran redwoodctl quick check, here's config:
Sam Support: ```
$ redwoodctl tenants get finedge
tenant: finedge
quota:
  rpm: 600
  tpm: 12000
  burst_window_seconds: 60
```
Kai Oncall: that aligns. If lots of clients hit exactly the same second (top of minute), they get folded into the same 60s window and exceed rpm briefly -> per-minute enforcement fires 429. Two fast remediations: temporary quota increase, or get customer to spread their heartbeats.
Priya Eng: okay please grab a request-per-second heatmap for the last 30m, 1s buckets.
Sam Support: metric query used:
Sam Support: ```sql
SELECT date_trunc('second', timestamp) AS t, count(*) as reqs
FROM requests
WHERE tenant='finedge' AND timestamp > now() - interval '30 minutes'
GROUP BY t
ORDER BY t desc
LIMIT 60;
```
Sam Support: results show clear spikes at :00 each minute with ~10-11 reqs/sec for that second and near 0 the rest of the minute.
Priya Eng: ok short-term I'll apply a 1h quota bump to avoid customer outage while we coordinate changes.
deploy-bot: QuotaChange(tenant=finedge): rpm 600 -> 1200, tpm 12000 -> 24000, duration=1h applied by priya.eng at 2026-03-17T09:22:30Z :white_check_mark:
Kai Oncall: monitoring for ingress and latency increases. I added an alert if cluster ingress > 5%.
Sam Support: notified customer: "Temporary quota increased for 1h. Recommend jittering heartbeat or using keepalive streaming instead of reconnect per minute. We can share snippet."
FinEdge (via DM): thanks, please send the snippet.
Anne CS: I'll send a short SDK snippet and doc links. Proposed snippet (python):
Anne CS: ```python
import random
import time

def heartbeat_loop():
    base_interval = 60
    jitter = random.uniform(0, 20)  # spread up to 20s
    sleep_time = base_interval + jitter
    while True:
        send_heartbeat()
        time.sleep(sleep_time)
```
Anne CS: and for fleets, we recommend per-process random offset on startup: time.sleep(random.uniform(0,60)) before first tick.
Priya Eng: also suggested guidance: use persistent streaming RPC where possible to avoid reconnect storms (streaming sessions keep socket alive and send pings), and if clients must reconnect, implement exponential backoff with cap.
Kai Oncall: ops follow-ups: 1) add a tenant-level per-second concentration graph to Console, 2) detect top-of-minute fanout patterns and surface a "jitter recommended" flag in tenant insights, 3) consider small automatic short-term quota bump if sudden symmetric spikes are detected (needs PO approval).
Sam Support: created customer ticket linking back to this thread and attached snippet.
Priya Eng: filing engineering ticket to create auto-detect rule and dashboard: ENG-5643.
Sam Support: marking as "mitigated" while bump is active. Will monitor and close after 1h if no recurrence. :thumbsup:
Kai Oncall: confirm no cascading errors. keeping thread open until 10:30 UTC.
Anne CS: sent snippet and a short playbook: jitter + avoid synchronized sleeps + use streaming pings. Customer acknowledged and will roll out jitter this afternoon.
Sam Support: resolved (temporary remedy). follow-up: postmortem if we see repeat. :white_check_mark:
